description:
Found by the fz-kdt.152 build (2026-09-02). PRE-EXISTING: identical at 62b5b09fe and after fz-kdt.152's fix, so it is a distinct root.

  fn main() do
    send(self(), fn (x) -> dbg(x * 2) end)
    f = receive do g -> g end
    Enum.each([1, 2, 3], f)
  end

interp prints 2/4/6 (correct). JIT and AOT print the FIRST element only and
then abort:

  fz_closure_get_capture_atom closure: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(4), found: ValueKind(13) }
  (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1777) -- panic in a function that cannot unwind

ValueKind(4) is CLOSURE and ValueKind(13) is INT, so the native side reads a
capture slot expecting the closure it stored and finds the element instead:
a capture-lane/ABI mismatch on the each path specifically. Enum.map,
Enum.filter and Enum.reduce with the same mailbox callable are correct on all
three doors after fz-kdt.152 (pinned by fixtures2/behavior/mailbox_closure_reduce.fz
and mailbox_closure_enum_hofs.fz); each is the one HOF still red, and it is
red only at the native door, which is why fz-kdt.152 could not pin it as a
companion.

Third three-path parity break in the closures x mailbox intersection
(fz-kdt.130, fz-kdt.152). Suspect Enum.each's own wrapper closure -- each
discards the reducer result, so its lambda's capture surface differs from
map's; compare against Prim::ClosureCapture's repr-from-the-storing-boundary
rule (fz-kdt.125/.128).
title: P1: a mailbox closure passed to Enum.each aborts on JIT and AOT
